source_metadata.title: Effects of Losartan on Renal and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes and Nephropathy
source_metadata.source_type: journal article; randomized double-blind placebo-controlled clinical trial
source_metadata.trial_name: RENAAL (Reduction of Endpoints in NIDDM with the Angiotensin II Antagonist Losartan)

atoms.canonical_statement: The RENAAL trial assessed whether losartan could delay doubling of serum creatinine, end-stage renal disease, or death in patients with type 2 diabetes and nephropathy, while also evaluating cardiovascular outcomes, proteinuria, and renal-disease progression.
RENAAL was an investigator-initiated, multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial conducted at 250 centers in 28 countries.
Eligible participants were 31-70 years old with type 2 diabetes and nephropathy defined by substantial albuminuria/proteinuria plus serum creatinine within prespecified ranges.

population.label: Randomized adults aged 31-70 years with type 2 diabetes and overt nephropathy
inclusion_criteria: Type 2 diabetes
Nephropathy with urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio at least 300 or urinary protein excretion at least 0.5 g/day
Serum creatinine 1.3-3.0 mg/dL, with lower limit 1.5 mg/dL for men weighing more than 60 kg
exclusion_criteria: Type 1 diabetes or nondiabetic renal disease, including renal-artery stenosis
Recent major cardiovascular events/procedures as prespecified
Any history of heart failure before enrollment

atoms.canonical_statement: Key exclusions included type 1 diabetes, nondiabetic renal disease including renal-artery stenosis, recent major cardiovascular events or revascularization, and any history of heart failure before enrollment.

atoms.canonical_statement: A total of 1513 patients were randomized: 751 to losartan and 762 to placebo; mean age was 60 years in both groups, approximately 63% were men, and mean baseline serum creatinine was 1.9 mg/dL.

atoms.canonical_statement: Losartan was started at 50 mg once daily and could be increased to 100 mg once daily to reach a blood-pressure target below 140/90 mm Hg; 71% of losartan-treated patients received 100 mg daily.

exposures.details: Dose increased to 100 mg once daily after 4 weeks if seated trough blood pressure remained above target; background conventional antihypertensive therapy allowed, excluding ACE inhibitors and other ARBs.

atoms.canonical_statement: The control group received placebo with conventional antihypertensive therapy; ACE inhibitors and other angiotensin-II receptor antagonists were excluded during randomized treatment.

exposures.details: Placebo equivalent with background conventional antihypertensive therapy; ACE inhibitors and other ARBs excluded by protocol.

atoms.canonical_statement: Randomization was stratified by baseline proteinuria, and primary/secondary endpoint analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle using Cox regression with baseline proteinuria as a stratification factor and geographic region as a covariate.

The trial was stopped early by a unanimous treatment-blinded steering committee because new external evidence suggested ACE inhibitors might reduce cardiovascular events in patients with renal impairment; mean follow-up was 3.4 years (range 2.3-4.6).

The primary endpoint was time to first occurrence of doubling of baseline serum creatinine, end-stage renal disease, or death; creatinine doubling required confirmation at least 4 weeks later, and end-stage renal disease was defined as long-term dialysis or renal transplantation.

concept.text: Primary composite: doubling of serum creatinine, end-stage renal disease, or death

outcome.definition: First occurrence of confirmed doubling of baseline serum creatinine, long-term dialysis or renal transplantation, or death.

atoms.canonical_statement: The prespecified cardiovascular secondary composite included myocardial infarction, stroke, first hospitalization for heart failure or unstable angina, coronary or peripheral revascularization, or cardiovascular death.

outcome.definition: Myocardial infarction, stroke, first hospitalization for heart failure or unstable angina, coronary or peripheral revascularization, or cardiovascular death.

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary composite endpoint occurred in 327/751 losartan patients (43.5%) and 359/762 placebo patients (47.1%); losartan reduced risk by 16% (95% CI 2%-28%; P=0.02).

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors reported that losartan was generally well tolerated and that adding losartan to conventional antihypertensive therapy did not increase adverse events overall.
The trial did not directly compare losartan with an ACE inhibitor, so the authors considered extrapolation between these drug classes speculative.

The authors noted that the lack of a significant cardiovascular composite benefit may partly reflect the relatively small sample for cardiovascular outcomes and enrollment criteria that excluded patients at high cardiovascular risk, including heart failure.
The authors concluded that losartan significantly improved renal outcomes beyond what could be attributed to blood-pressure control in patients with type 2 diabetes and nephropathy.
The study was supported by Merck and Company.

The disclosure section reported multiple consulting, research-grant, and speakers-bureau relationships with pharmaceutical companies among academic authors; three authors (Snapinn, Zhang, and Shahinfar) were Merck employees and could own Merck stock or options.
